Subject: Billing options after trial - invoice vs card?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the trial — usage looked good and the team wants to move to a paid plan. Before we commit, quick clarifying questions on billing:

- Do you support monthly invoicing for Hosted API (we'd prefer an invoice and PO rather than a corporate card)?
- What net terms are available (Net 30/Net 45)? Is a signed enterprise contract required for net terms or can we do net 30 on a standard TOS + PO?
- Any minimums or credit checks we should be aware of?
- Also: do you offer any onboarding or consumption discounts if we commit to a 12-month usage baseline?

Our procurement address is procurement@edenai.com — happy to route docs there. Goal is to get billing sorted this week so we can flip to paid traffic.

Best,

Subject: Re: Billing options after trial - invoice vs card?

Hi Olivia — great to hear the trial hit the right signals. Short answers up front, then next steps:

- Yes: we support card payments (instant) and monthly invoicing (paper invoice + ACH/wire) for Hosted API.
- Net terms: Net 30 is the standard option for approved customers; Net 45 can be considered for larger enterprise accounts with legal review.
- Requirements for Net 30: signed order form or PO, completed procurement form, and a simple billing setup call. For accounts above our credit threshold we run a quick credit check (manual, vendor-friendly).
- Discounts: we can offer a consumption discount for committed annual spends or a one-time onboarding credit. Ben has the details and will propose a specific structure below.

I've attached our Redwood_Invoice_Spec.pdf and a fillable Procurement_Form — if procurement sends that back to procurement@redwood.ai we can start the Net 30 approval flow.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) billing contact and PO cadence (monthly?), (b) expected monthly baseline $ value, and (c) whether you want the finance team to run a credit check? Once we have that, Ben/Finance can issue a formal quote + any commit discount.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0193

Subject: Re: Billing options after trial - invoice vs card?

Hi Olivia — looping in with a concrete proposal:

Option A (No commit, fastest):
- Card on file or monthly ACH by invoice. No minimums. No discount.

Option B (12-mo commit):
- Commit to $6,000/month baseline for 12 months (billed monthly).
- 10% off per-token rates on hosted API for committed usage; any overage billed at standard rates.
- Net 30 available after procurement form + PO + one-time credit check.

Option C (Quarterly prepay):
- Pay quarterly via invoice; 6% discount on prepayment. Net terms are not applicable for prepaid plans.

Deal details: deal_id RA-2026-0897. If you can send a PO referencing that deal id, procurement@edenai.com, we can attach it to the order form and begin Net 30 processing. Typical Net 30 approval turnaround is 3–5 business days once we receive a completed procurement form and W-9.

Happy to model numbers if you share rough consumption per month after trial.

—Ben

Tessa — quick finance summary:

- Minimum: We routinely approve Net 30 for invoices >= $3,000/month after basic checks. Below that, card-on-file is standard unless site credit approval is granted.
- Docs required: completed Procurement_Form, PO referencing the deal id (optional but preferred), W-9 (for US entities), and a short billing contact confirmation email. For accounts forecasted > $10k/month we request a basic credit check.
- Turnaround: 2–5 business days after receiving all docs.

I'll start the provisional Net 30 workflow as soon as procurement@edenai.com sends back the fillable form and the W-9. If procurement wants a template invoice or consolidated billing across multiple subsidiaries, let me know and I'll produce a sample.
